BLOCKER: s3store.ApplyLifecycle returns nil without applying anything when RetainUntil is set but Mode is empty (`if mode != ""` guard): a caller requesting retention gets success and no retention — silent fail-open of a compliance control.
MAJOR: objreconcile.notFound classifies errors via substring matching ("not found", "nosuchkey"); a permission/transient error containing those words is reported as `missing` instead of failing the scan — corrupts drift reports, and datastore exposes no typed NotFound to use instead.

objpolicy.Mint takes `tenantPrefix` as an untrusted parameter while the doc claims it "comes from the authenticated tenant context"; nothing enforces that — the central tenant guard is convention-only and trivially bypassed by passing a broad prefix.

S3 Capabilities advertises `ObjectLock: true` unconditionally even for buckets without object-lock; `datastore.Lifecycle()` then hands out a capability that fails at runtime with an untyped provider error instead of ErrUnsupported — no probe or ErrUnsupported mapping in ObjectLifecycle/GetRetention.

The single privilege boundary for signed URLs emits denials via stdlib `log.Printf` with no structured fields, request/tenant identity, or metrics — insufficient audit/observability for an authz decision point.

No docs/ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS or EDP-16 doc update accompanies the new central policy and reconciliation modules, despite the standards requiring decision records for shipped architectural boundaries.
MINOR: Scan's prefix guard is a raw `strings.HasPrefix(e.Key, prefix)`: an unprefixed/loose prefix (e.g. "p") admits cross-prefix keys ("px/…") into the manifest and masks them as valid.
Manifest entries flagged `Invalid` are excluded from `want`, so their corresponding store objects are additionally reported as `Orphaned` — the same manifest defect is double-counted as store drift.
S3 integration test defers `Delete` on an object still under 1h GOVERNANCE retention; the delete always fails silently and leaks a locked object into the bucket.
ApplyLifecycle applies retention then legal hold with no rollback on partial failure; `LegalHold && ReleaseLegalHold` silently resolves to release.
ObjectLifecycle issues a GetBucketVersioning call on every read (extra round-trip per object) and swallows the error.
Checksum comparison uses `strings.EqualFold` with no format/algorithm validation, so "sha256:aa" vs "aa" or wrong-length digests are classified as mismatches rather than invalid manifest input.
NIT: cleanPath rejects any key containing ".." after path.Clean (e.g. "a..b") — false denials for legitimate keys.
Mint checks the provider capability before method/TTL/tenant validation, so unsupported providers mask policy violations with ErrUnsupported.
`Schema = "pf.objreconcile/2"` starts at version 2 for a brand-new module; stub/fake ObjectStore implementations are duplicated across test packages.
Key equals tenantPrefix exactly is accepted (`k == prefix`), minting URLs for the tenant root itself.
SUMMARY: Solid structural fit: optional capability interface, typed ErrUnsupported, read-only deterministic reconcile report, and Go-only new logic all align with the acceptance criteria and standards.

Top risks: a fail-open retention path in S3 ApplyLifecycle, substring-based not-found classification corrupting drift reports, and a tenant guard that depends on caller discipline rather than authenticated context.
Secondary gaps: unprobed ObjectLock capability advertisement, weak audit logging at the signed-URL policy boundary, and missing ADR/doc updates for the new modules.
